title: After updating license specification a newer setuptool is required.
body:
I noticed that I needed a newer setuptools to install the newest ASE version in EasyBuild with foss/2025a toolchain.  It barfed over the new license specification and I had to pick a new setuptools as a build dependency.  According to the documentation, the new license specification is supported starting with version 77.0.3:

https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/guides/writing-pyproject-toml/#license-and-license-files

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body:
I don't understand the failed test:

`AssertionError: too many nonstdlib modules loaded: 261/200`

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
77.0 is from ~~May~~ March this year, so that's more recent than what we usually like to depend on.  But since we actually *do* depend on it, I suppose we should merge this.  Also, this is a lot more lightweight than e.g. numpy or scipy version.

To explain the issue, we don't want a "bare" `import ase` to load too many modules, so there's a test that will complain if for some reason we import more than we want to.  (The most obvious benefit of not importing so many modules is to avoid loading hundreds of files for a CLI autocomplete)

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body:
> 77.0 is from ~~May~~ March this year, so that's more recent than what we usually like to depend on. But since we actually _do_ depend on it, I suppose we should merge this.

Yes, that makes me a bit uncomfortable also, since even very new Python installations now come with a too old setuptools.  I hope that pip normally loads the newer setuptool, and hope that this will not break older packages.

An alternative would of course be to revert the change in the ``pyproject.toml`` file, but we may come to regret that later.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
The license specifications have been changed several times, as it's always a little bit of a circus where twine, pypi, setuptools, ..., each have opinions.

We should probably set up releases so they are done with the oldest libraries.  I'll make an issue.
